verdicts.location: apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EffectWorker.ts:263-271 (catch rethrows any error that is not turnCompleted); EffectWorker.ts:818-825 (outbox.fail after maxAttempts)
verdicts.summary: A steered question notice is only re-queued when the steer fails with turnCompleted. Any other steer failure while the turn is still running is retried five times and then fails, and the notice is never delivered. This is separate from finding [0] (model selection).
verdicts.scenario: 1) Parent run R1 is running on provider turn T1. An async question (responseCapability 'message') arrives. DelegatedTaskQuestionReactor.ts:43-58 dispatches it as queue_after_active; Orchestrator.ts:5739-5775 upgrades it to steer_active; dispatchSteerIntoRun (Orchestrator.ts:4961-4983) appends the notice as a notification turn item under R1 and enqueues provider-turn.steer. 2) When the effect runs, T1 is still 'running' but the steer fails for a non-completion reason: the session is missing from the registry (ProviderTurnControlService.ts:153-183, error at 177-182), the recorded provider target is invalid (ProviderTurnControlService.ts:112-124), or the provider's steer call fails (ProviderTurnControlService.ts:392-407 sets turnCompleted only when the turn is completed). 3) EffectWorker.ts:263-271 rethrows because turnCompleted is false. The executor retries with 100/200/400/800 ms backoff up to maxAttempts=5 (EffectWorker.ts:649, 786-833), then calls outbox.fail. 4) Nothing re-queues the notice. No handler exists for a failed provider-turn.steer (the only references are in EffectWorker.ts:234-332). Non-retryable handling covers only provider-turn.interrupt (EffectWorker.ts:47-57). The reactor does not re-wake an async question (DelegatedTaskQuestionReactor.ts:82-87 skips non-live requests in the catch-up).
verdicts.consequence: The notice card appears under R1 but the parent never gets a follow-up turn, so the child's async question stays unanswered with no error shown. Before this commit the same question was queued (DelegatedTaskQuestionReactor.ts:55 is unchanged) and started a run, so it could not be lost this way.

verdicts.location: apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EffectWorker.ts:298-300 and 316-330 (retry dispatch; catchTags only handles the disabled error); ThreadManagementService.ts:707-716 (dispatch-time instance check)
verdicts.summary: The retry dispatch goes through the dispatch-time instance check, which the original queued dispatch did not face after it was queued. If the thread's provider instance is disabled between the steer and the retry, the notice is dropped. The note's failure_mode accepts this drop as 'the result stands', which holds for mailbox completions but not for a question.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A question notice is steered into a running parent turn. The initial dispatch passes assertDispatchTargetEnabled, which checks the thread's selection (ThreadManagementService.ts:707-716). 2) Before the steer effect runs, the user disables that provider instance. 3) The steer loses the race (turnCompleted). The retry at EffectWorker.ts:286-315 has no modelSelection for notifications, so ThreadManagementService.dispatch re-runs assertDispatchTargetEnabled against the thread's selection and fails with ThreadManagementProviderInstanceDisabledError. 4) EffectWorker.ts:317-329 logs 'steer-follow-up-disabled' and drops the retry. The notice never starts a follow-up turn. Before this commit, the question was queued at dispatch and started later from the queue, without a second dispatch-time instance check. I read only the dispatch-side check, not the queued-run start path.
verdicts.consequence: The question notice is silently dropped with only an info-level log. The child's question goes unanswered by the parent. This is a narrow window (a provider disabled during a steer race).

verdicts.summary: A steer can target a provider turn that has already completed while the run is still running (continuingRun). The steer then reaches the provider, and a silent acceptance is treated as delivered for a notification, with no retry and no delivery receipt.
verdicts.scenario: The provider turn T1 completes, but the run's activeAttemptId still matches and the run is running, so continuingRun is true (ProviderTurnControlService.ts:133-135). The steer is not rejected at 136-145 and goes to the provider with T1's id (ProviderTurnControlService.ts:392-408). If the provider accepts the input without applying it to a live turn, EffectWorker.ts:246-261 records no delivery.accept for a notification-only message, and nothing re-queues it.
verdicts.consequence: A question notice could be accepted by the provider and never shown to the model, with no retry and no error. Whether this happens depends on the provider adapter's steer-on-completed-turn behaviour, which is not in this checkout.
verdicts.missing: The provider adapters' (Codex, Claude, ACP) behaviour when turn/steer is sent with a completed turn id while the run is still running. Whether an accepted steer is always applied to a live turn is decided there.
